meta.title: Seventeen services need a new certificate within 30 days

slides.title: Seventeen services need a new certificate within 30 days
body: A scan of every service endpoint found nine expired certificates and eight more that expire within a month. Most of the risk sits where renewal is still done by hand.
sources: Certificate scan of the service catalogue, 20 October 2026; Monitoring alert rules, exported 21 October 2026

slides.title: Renew the nine expired certificates this week
body: Then move the 30 services that renew by hand onto automatic renewal before December.
Counts: 17 of 140 services need action: 9 expired, 8 expire within 30 days. Three findings: one high, one medium, one low.
Fix first: the expired certificates (finding 1); Platform has the most, with five to renew.
Then: automatic renewal for the Data and Mobile teams, who renew 20 of the 30 manual certificates.
sources: Certificate scan of the service catalogue, 20 October 2026; Monitoring alert rules, exported 21 October 2026

slides.title: Seventeen of 140 services need action within a month
body: Every service presents a Transport Layer Security (TLS) certificate that proves who it is to its callers. When one expires, callers that check it refuse to connect, and the service is down for them even though it is running.
The figures here are counts.

stats.label: callers that check will refuse them

slides.title: Expiry comes from manual renewal and late alerts
body: High: Nine certificates have already expired
Medium: Two teams renew most certificates by hand
slides.notes: Findings run from most to least severe.

slides.title: Nine certificates have already expired
body: Where: mobile-web, mobile-worker, platform-admin-4, search-web-3, payments-web, platform-notify-4, accounts-reports, platform-cache, platform-search
Evidence: The scan read an expiry date before 22 October on each. The oldest expired 28 days ago.
Impact: Any caller that verifies the certificate fails to connect. Callers that skip verification still connect, which is why some of these went unnoticed.
Fix: Renew each one, then confirm with a second scan of those endpoints.
sources: Certificate scan of the service catalogue, 20 October 2026; Monitoring alert rules, exported 21 October 2026

slides.title: Two teams renew most certificates by hand
body: Where: Data (9 of 19 services) and Mobile (11 of 24)
Evidence: 20 of the 30 manual renewals belong to these two teams.
Impact: A renewal that depends on a person's calendar fails when that person is away.
Fix: Move both teams to the automatic renewal the other four teams use.
sources: Certificate scan of the service catalogue, 20 October 2026; Monitoring alert rules, exported 21 October 2026

slides.title: The other finding is low severity
slides.notes: The only alert fires after a certificate expires. Where: Monitoring rules for all services Evidence: The certificate alert triggers on a failed handshake, which happens only once the certificate has expired. Impact: Owners learn of an expiry from their callers. Fix: Add a warning at 30 days and a page at 7 days.

slides.title: The scan checked every endpoint once, from inside the network
body: Each service endpoint in the service catalogue was contacted once on 20 October 2026, from a host inside the network, and its certificate's expiry date, issuer and renewal setting were recorded. Days left are counted from 22 October. Services were matched to teams by the catalogue's owner field.

slides.title: Three things this audit did not check
body: Certificates used between services inside a cluster, which the platform rotates on its own schedule.
Certificates on third-party services we call.
Whether each caller verifies certificates at all.
